newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GLAVINE REPORTED AGREEING TO $42 MILLION DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GLAVINE REPORTED AGREEING TO $42 MILLION DEAL.

text.p: Atlanta Braves left-hander Tom Glavine has agreed to a five-year, $42 million contract extension that would make him baseball's highest-paid pitcher, the ESPN cable television network reported Wednesday.
ESPN said the contract includes a $4 million signing bonus and that the deal was expected to be announced Thursday, ending the possibility of him becoming a free agent.
The 31-year-old Glavine has 121 wins in the 1990s, more than any pitcher except teammate Greg Maddux (125). He is in the final year of a five-year deal that pays him $5 million this season.
The annual average of Glavine's reported deal is $8.4 million, exceeding the contracts given to teammate John Smoltz and Roger Clemens of the Toronto Blue Jays.

Smoltz, who won the 1996 National League Cy Young Award, was re-signed for $31 million over four years. Clemens, a three-time American League Cy Young Award winner, left the Boston Red Sox and signed a three-year, $24.75 million deal with Toronto.
Glavine won the 1991 Cy Young and was runner-up to Maddux in 1992 before finishing third for three straight years. He is 5-2 with a 2.08 ERA this year and has a career mark of 144-94 with a 3.41 ERA.

Once completed, the contract would leave Maddux as the only member of the Braves' rotation, generally considered the major leagues' best, who is not signed to a long-term deal. Maddux, who has won a record four Cy Young Awards, can become a free agent at the end of the season but is expected to be re-signed.
